paper_title: SepLLM Accelerate Large Language Models by Compressing One Segment into   One Separator
caption_used: Training loss curves over iterations for Vanilla, StrmLLM (n=64), and four SepLLM configurations. All models start with loss values exceeding 3.4 and converge as training progresses to 140,000 iterations. The Vanilla model achieves the lowest final loss at approximately 2.45, while StrmLLM (n=64) converges to roughly 2.60, showing a notable gap from the SepLLM variants. Among the SepLLM configurations, the H/T variant reaches the lowest loss at approximately 2.49, with SepLLM (n=128) settling at approximately 2.55, slightly above both the base SepLLM (n=64) and SepLLM (n=64, H) which converge near 2.51-2.52. The most rapid decrease in loss occurs within the first 20,000 iterations for all models, after which convergence slows considerably.
model_annotation: The plot illustrates the training loss curves over iterations for six different models: Vanilla, StrmLLM (n=64), and four SepLLM configurations, including SepLLM (n=64), SepLLM (n=64, H), SepLLM (n=64, H/T), and SepLLM (n=128). The x-axis represents the number of iterations, with a linear scale ranging from 0 to 140,000 in intervals of 20,000. The y-axis represents the loss, with a linear scale ranging from 2.4 to 3.4 in intervals of 0.1. The plot contains six lines, each representing a different model. The purple line for Vanilla starts above 3.3 and decreases to approximately 2.45. The blue line for StrmLLM (n=64) starts above 3.3 and decreases to roughly 2.60. The orange line for SepLLM (n=64) starts above 3.3 and decreases to approximately 2.51. The green line for SepLLM (n=64, H) starts above 3.3 and decreases to approximately 2.52. The red line for SepLLM (n=64, H/T) starts above 3.3 and decreases to approximately 2.49. The dark blue line for SepLLM (n=128) starts above 3.3 and decreases to approximately 2.55. All lines exhibit a rapid decline in loss within the first 20,000 iterations, followed by a gradual convergence.
